newsitem.title: CANADA: Alcan plans to invest in B.C. despite suit.
newsitem.headline: Alcan plans to invest in B.C. despite suit.

text.p: Alcan Aluminium Ltd said on Tuesday that it plans continue to invest in British Columbia despite its C$535 million-plus lawsuit against the western Canadian province.
"We will reinvest in B.C. any compensation from the lawsuit," Alcan spokesman Dan Gagne told a press conference.

On Monday, Alcan filed a lawsuit against B.C. seeking compensation for the company's investment in the Kemano Completion Project, which the province cancelled in January 1995. Alcan had spent C$535 million on the project, which would have increased its hydro-electric power generating capacity.
Alcan wrote down the cost of the Kemano project in third-quarter 1995 and has said it would treat any compensation received as an extraordinary gain.

Gagne said Alcan and the province had not been able to resolve the issue of the economic value of Kemano, including the amount above the C$535 million cost of the abandoned project that would be needed "to make Alcan whole."

Gagne said any estimate of the economic value of the project could range from "zero to a billion dollars," but added that in his comments on Monday, B.C. Premier Glen Clark appeared to suggest that Kemano had no economic value.
Alcan legal counsel Lorne Peterson said there was a "grand canyon" between what the company and the province think had been taken away from Alcan in cancelling the Kemano project.
"We are looking for compensation for what we have lost," Peterson said.
